title: Leela Enterprises v. Prakash Brothers
text: This revision petition challenges the conviction of the petitioner under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. The cheque of Rs 6,75,000 was dishonoured with the remark 'Drawer's Signature Differs'. The revisionist argues that signature mismatch does not constitute dishonour within the meaning of the Negotiable Instruments Act. This High Court, however, notes that dishonour of a cheque on any technical ground, including signature mismatch, falls within the ambit of Section 138 NI Act as interpreted by the Supreme Court in several decisions. The complainant's evidence that the cheque was issued for a legally enforceable debt stands unrebutted. The drawer offered no plausible explanation for the signature discrepancy. The court upholds the conviction of the drawer. The sentence of fine of Rs 13,50,000 is confirmed. The revision petition is dismissed. The drawer is held guilty as convicted by the trial court.
